blocks.text: Exercise 1. a) ⁧أَمْن⁩ : alif (start word), amn · b) ⁧إِرْهَاب⁩ : alif, hamza under the i, irhāb · c) ⁧سُؤَال⁩ : wāw (u previous stronger than a), suʾāl · d) ⁧رَئِيس⁩ : yāʾ (The hamza has the i), raʾīs · e) ⁧مَسْؤُول⁩ : wāw (the hamza has the u; First there is sukūn), masʾūl · f) ⁧شَيْء⁩ : line (end word after sukūn), šayʾ · g) ⁧مَاء⁩ : line (end word after ā), māʾ · h) ⁧لَاجِئ⁩ : yāʾ (end word after i), lāǧiʾ · i) ⁧مُؤْتَمَر⁩ : wāw (u previous), muʾtamar · j) ⁧قَرَأَ⁩ : alif (a), qaraʾa Exercise 2. a) ʾamal (hope) · b) ʿamal (work) · c) saʾala (he asked) · d) saʿala (coughed) · e) amn · f) ʿadad · g) raʾīs · h) šaʿb Exercise 3. a) ʿalā · b) ʿAlī · c) ilā · d) mustašfā · e) fī · f) hāḏā · g) lākin · h) āḫir Exercise 4. a) kitābun → kitāb · b) kitāban → kitābā (in the classic pause; in common use often kitāban) · c) kitābin → kitāb · d) madīnatan → madīna · e) šukran (adverb: stays šukran) · f) ǧiddan (rest ǧiddan) · g) māʾan → māʾā / māʾ · h) baytun → bayt Exercise 5. a) wa-l-yawm · b) f l-madīnati · c) wa-š-šurṭa · d) ismī · e) wa-smī · f) bi-smo llāhi Exercise 6. a) ⁧أَمْن⁩ · b) ⁧رَئِيس⁩ · c) ⁧سُؤَال⁩ · d) ⁧شَيْء⁩ · e) ⁧مَاء⁩ · f) ⁧عَلَى⁩ · g) ⁧شُكْرًا⁩ · h) ⁧آخِر⁩ Exercise 7. a) muʾtamar, conference b) masʾūl, responsible, official · c) lāǧiʾ, refugee · d) irhābterrorism. e) mustašfā, hospital · f) aḫbār, News Exercise 8. a) ⁧هٰذَا⁩ hāḏā · ⁧لٰكِنْ⁩ lākin · ⁧مَسْؤُول⁩ masʾūl · ⁧رَئِيس⁩ raʾīs · ⁧أَخْبَار⁩ aḫbār · ⁧مُسْتَشْفَى⁩ mustašfā. b) ʿalā l- maktab, on the office / on the desk: Egyptian press often writes ⁧ى⁩ as ⁧ي⁩ no points or vice versa; name ʿAlī followed by the office (s) would not form a sentence. c) No, I'm the same word. masʾūl, written according to two conventions (the Egyptian with ⁧ئ⁩ ). 1. On alif: ⁧أ⁩ with a or u, ⁧إ⁩ with i.
2. In ⁧رَئِيس⁩ the hamza has the kasra (i, the strongest vowel): ⁧ئ⁩ . In ⁧سُؤَال⁩ the previous vowel is u, stronger than a
5. An alif that is pronounced only at the beginning of the sentence and falls after a vowel; for example the article: al-bayt / wa-l-
6. hāḏā: ā is indicated by a short breath above the ⁧ه⁩ , that in texts without vowels is not written.
